cues.en: This is The Happy Pod from the BBC World Service.
cues.zh: 这里是 BBC 世界服务的《快乐播客》。

cues.en: I'm Holly Gibbs, and in this edition...
cues.zh: 我是 Holly Gibbs，本期节目将带来……

cues.en: We've always had a deep bond, but now with this tattoo, it almost feels magical, and it's just the most incredible feeling in the world.
cues.zh: 我们一直有着深厚的羁绊，但有了这个纹身后，感觉几乎像魔法一样，这是世上最不可思议的感受。

cues.en: How one mother's tattoo has opened up a new world of communication for her son.
cues.zh: 一位母亲的纹身如何为她的儿子打开了全新的沟通世界。

cues.en: Also on this podcast, the regatta where all the participants are breast cancer survivors.
cues.zh: 本期还将介绍一场特别的赛艇会，所有参赛者都是乳腺癌幸存者。

cues.en: We joke all the time that we're all in the same boat, literally. We have differences across everything else, and then there's this one major thing that binds us all.
cues.zh: 我们总开玩笑说，字面意义上我们都在同一条船上。除此之外，我们各不相同，但有一件大事把我们所有人联系在一起。

cues.en: Plus the nursery which operates inside a retirement home, and a world first.
cues.zh: 此外，还有一家开在养老院里的托儿所，以及一项全球首创。

cues.en: The AI acted as a sort of co-pilot assistant adjacent to the primary screen, identifying the structures that we care most about.
cues.zh: 人工智能像副驾驶助手一样位于主屏幕旁，识别出我们最关注的结构。

cues.en: How AI was used to help successfully remove a tumour near the brain.
cues.zh: 人工智能如何帮助医生成功切除脑部附近的肿瘤。

cues.en: A mother in Canada has come up with a unique way to communicate with her autistic child.
cues.zh: 加拿大一位母亲想出了与自闭症孩子沟通的独特方式。

cues.en: Jessica Fletcher has a keyboard tattooed on her forearm, which her non-speaking son Hunter uses to talk to her.
cues.zh: Jessica Fletcher 在前臂上纹了一副键盘，她不会说话的儿子 Hunter 用它与她交流。

cues.en: She posted it online in a video which has been viewed millions of times, and has even inspired other parents to get the same design.
cues.zh: 她把这件事拍成视频发布到网上，观看次数已达数百万，甚至还启发其他家长纹上同样的图案。

cues.en: I caught up with Jessica.
cues.zh: 我采访了 Jessica。

cues.en: My son, Hunter, he's 11 years old, and he was diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder when he was three.
cues.zh: 我儿子 Hunter 今年11岁，三岁时被诊断为自闭症谱系障碍。

cues.en: At a very young age, he started communicating with a system called PECS, and that's where he would just get pictures and bring them to me.
cues.zh: 他很小的时候就开始使用一种叫 PECS 的系统沟通：拿来图片，再把图片带给我。

cues.en: And that turned into him using an AAC device, which is an iPad with symbols, and it speaks for him.
cues.zh: 后来他开始使用 AAC 设备，也就是一台带有符号的 iPad，由它替他发声。

cues.en: And he's just the light of my life. He is the most beautiful thing about my life.
cues.zh: 他就是我生命中的光，是我生命中最美好的存在。

cues.en: Can you describe your tattoo?
cues.zh: 你能描述一下你的纹身吗？

cues.en: Yeah, so my tattoo is just a basic keyboard layout.
cues.zh: 好，我的纹身就是一个基本的键盘布局。

cues.en: There's no punctuation or no numbers, but there is a space bar, there's a yes and a no button.
cues.zh: 上面没有标点符号，也没有数字，但有空格键，还有“是”和“否”按钮。

cues.en: There's also an I love you button, and there is a happy face and a sad face.
cues.zh: 还有“我爱你”按钮，以及笑脸和哭脸。

cues.en: And it's on my left forearm because it's easier for him to reach and easier for me to read.
cues.zh: 它纹在我的左前臂上，因为这样他更容易够到，我也更容易看清。

cues.en: It's so funny because I have to look at it closely to tell what he's reading,
cues.zh: 这很有趣，因为我得仔细看，才能知道他读的是哪一部分，

cues.en: but he can type on it if he's standing to my left and it's upside down to him.
cues.zh: 但如果他站在我的左边，即使键盘对他来说是倒过来的，他也能在上面打字。

cues.en: Where did the idea come from?
cues.zh: 这个想法是怎么来的？

cues.en: Hunter loves to swim. That's his main hobby.
cues.zh: Hunter 喜欢游泳，那是他的主要爱好。

cues.en: And he has always struggled with not being able to communicate in the water, because he can't take his device in the water.
cues.zh: 他一直苦于无法在水里沟通，因为不能把设备带进水中。

cues.en: So I've made communication boards that were waterproof. It wasn't convenient, and it wasn't accessible enough.
cues.zh: 所以我做过防水的沟通板，但既不方便，也不够易于使用。

cues.en: So I've always been trying to come up with a new way.
cues.zh: 所以我一直在想办法找出新的方式。

cues.en: One day, we went to a restaurant, and his device died,
cues.zh: 有一天，我们去了餐厅，他的设备没电了，

cues.en: and I started writing the alphabet, because at school, one of his teachers has an alphabet board up, and I've seen him finger spell on it.
cues.zh: 我就开始写字母表，因为他学校的一位老师挂着字母板，我见过他在上面用手指拼写。

cues.en: Well, Hunter got mad at me, flipped the paper over, and started writing the keyboard layout.
cues.zh: 结果 Hunter 生我的气，把纸翻过来，开始写键盘布局。

cues.en: That's because he's learned to type on a keyboard, because he likes to Google things to show me what he wants.
cues.zh: 这是因为他学会了在键盘上打字，他喜欢把想要的东西搜出来给我看。

cues.en: So that was kind of the aha moment, and I was like, okay, a keyboard, that's clearly his favourite way to communicate.
cues.zh: 那一刻我恍然大悟：好，键盘显然是他最喜欢的沟通方式。

cues.en: And then I thought, how can I make this so we'd never forget it at home, so it's waterproof, and the battery doesn't die.
cues.zh: 然后我想，怎样才能让我们在家永远不会忘记它，让它防水，而且电池不会没电？

cues.en: And then that's where the idea of a tattoo came.
cues.zh: 于是，纹身这个想法就产生了。

cues.en: And how has it helped Hunter?
cues.zh: 这个纹身对 Hunter 有什么帮助？

cues.en: It's helped tremendously.
cues.zh: 帮助非常大。

cues.en: A lot of kids with autism struggle with physical touch, and this has kind of taught Hunter what safe touch means.
cues.zh: 很多自闭症孩子不适应身体接触，而这个纹身算是让 Hunter 明白了什么是安全的触碰。

cues.en: So now I'm getting a lot more affection, a lot more hugs.
cues.zh: 所以现在他对我表达了更多亲昵，也拥抱我更多。

cues.en: He says, I love you, a lot more often. It's also given him the ability to speak to me privately,
cues.zh: 他说“我爱你”的次数多多了。这个纹身还让他能够私下和我交流，

cues.en: because when he uses the device, the whole room hears what he's saying.
cues.zh: 因为他使用设备时，整个房间的人都会听见他说的话。

cues.en: Do you have a favourite memory of him using it?
cues.zh: 你最喜欢他使用纹身的哪段记忆是什么？

cues.en: Definitely the first day I got it.
cues.zh: 当然是我拿到纹身的第一天。

cues.en: He grabbed my arm and made such direct eye contact, which he does when he sees something that's visually stimulating to him.
cues.zh: 他抓住我的手臂，直直地看着我；看到视觉上吸引他的东西时，他就会这样。

cues.en: And he wrote mama on my arm.
cues.zh: 然后他在我的手臂上写下了“妈妈”。

cues.en: Later that night, a couple hours later, I think he really had time to process and realized that it was permanent and it was all for him.
cues.zh: 那天晚上过了几个小时，我想他终于有时间消化这件事，意识到纹身是永久的，而且这一切都是为他做的。

cues.en: And he said, "I love you, Mama," on it.
cues.zh: 然后他在上面写道：“妈妈，我爱你。”

cues.en: How do you feel when he uses it? That must be a really special feeling.
cues.zh: 他使用纹身时，你有什么感受？那一定是非常特别的感受。

cues.en: It's just, we've always had a deep bond, but now with this tattoo, it almost feels magical, and it's just the most incredible feeling in the world.
cues.zh: 我们一直感情深厚，但有了这个纹身，一切几乎变得不可思议。这是世界上最奇妙的感受。

cues.en: It's crazy that something as—I mean,
cues.zh: 这太不可思议了——我的意思是，

cues.en: It's not simple, but it is. It's crazy something just a tattoo has opened up this world of communication for you both.
cues.zh: 它并不简单，但又确实简单。难以想象，仅仅一个纹身就为你们俩打开了沟通的新世界。

cues.en: Yeah, it is. And a lot of parents have reached out. I have photos of at least a dozen parents that have gone and gotten the same tattoo.
cues.zh: 是的。很多家长联系了我，至少有十几位家长已经去做了一模一样的纹身，我还收到了他们的照片。

cues.en: There's tattoo artists all over the world that are offering to do it for free for parents in need.
cues.zh: 世界各地的纹身师都愿意为有需要的家长免费制作这个纹身。

cues.en: I've heard from artists in the United States, in the United Kingdom, in Ireland, and in Australia, and it's just crazy how global it's gotten.
cues.zh: 美国、英国、爱尔兰和澳大利亚的纹身师都联系过我，真没想到它会传播到全世界。

cues.en: And so we created shirts with it on the sleeve for people that don't want a tattoo.
cues.zh: 所以我们把这个图案印在衣袖上做成衣服，给不想纹身的人穿。

cues.en: And it's not just the autism community that's interested.
cues.zh: 感兴趣的不只是自闭症群体。

cues.en: I've had nurses that work with patients that have lost their ability to speak reach out about it.
cues.zh: 也有帮助失去说话能力的患者的护士联系我。

cues.en: First responders are reaching out about it.
cues.zh: 急救人员也联系了我。

cues.en: It's really opening a lot of doors and opening a lot of conversations about communication barriers.
cues.zh: 它确实打开了许多大门，也引发了很多关于沟通障碍的讨论。

cues.en: I guess there's a message here, isn't there, about going out of your way to help people who can't communicate through words.
cues.zh: 我想这传达了一个信息：我们应该主动帮助那些无法用语言沟通的人。

cues.en: Why is it important that we do find ways to communicate with everybody?
cues.zh: 为什么我们一定要找到与每个人沟通的方式？

cues.en: Historically, we've often brushed off non-speakers. There's been this long-time assumption that non-speaking means non-thinking, and that's not true.
cues.zh: 过去，我们多少忽视了不说话的人。长期以来，人们以为不会说话就不会思考，但事实并非如此。

cues.en: Just because they can't speak, they have a whole world of thoughts and feelings and complex ideas inside of them.
cues.zh: 他们只是无法说话，但内心拥有完整的思想、感受和复杂的想法。

cues.en: You spoke a minute ago just about the reaction that you've had when you posted this tattoo online.
cues.zh: 你刚才谈到了把这个纹身发到网上后得到的反响。

cues.en: How does it feel to know that you're inspiring that change for other families?
cues.zh: 知道自己正在为其他家庭带来这样的改变，你感觉如何？

cues.en: It feels really incredible. I didn't expect it to go this viral. Like to see that it has over 115 million views is wild.
cues.zh: 感觉真的不可思议。我没想到它会这么火。看到浏览量超过1.15亿，简直太疯狂了。

cues.en: I knew in this life that my purpose was Hunter, but I've always wanted to make an impact in the world and make a difference for other families.
cues.zh: 我知道此生的使命就是陪伴亨特，但我一直也想影响这个世界，为其他家庭带来改变。

cues.en: The main message I like to tell people is to always presume competence.
cues.zh: 我最想告诉大家的是：永远要假定他们有能力。

cues.en: Don't talk about them, talk to them.
cues.zh: 不要谈论他们，要和他们交谈。

cues.en: Don't assume that they aren't as intelligent as you are, because 99% of the time, they are.
cues.zh: 不要以为他们不如你聪明，因为99%的时候，他们和你一样聪明。

cues.en: That was Jessica Fletcher. To the French Alps next, where a regatta is taking place in Aix-les-Bains.
cues.zh: 刚才是杰西卡·弗莱彻。接下来前往法国阿尔卑斯山，艾克斯莱班正在举行一场赛艇比赛。

cues.en: This, however, is a festival with a difference.
cues.zh: 不过，这是一场与众不同的节庆活动。

cues.en: All the participants in the dragon boat race are survivors of breast cancer.
cues.zh: 龙舟赛的所有参赛者都是乳腺癌幸存者。

cues.en: The event is run by the International Breast Cancer Paddlers' Commission, and one of the women taking part is Maria Fleming.
cues.zh: 活动由国际乳腺癌划船者委员会主办，参赛者之一是玛丽亚·弗莱明。

cues.en: She belongs to the Irish group, the Plurabelle Paddlers. She spoke to me from the event.
cues.zh: 她来自爱尔兰的 Plurabelle Paddlers 队，并在活动现场接受了我的采访。

cues.en: I was diagnosed in 2019, and I was 49 at the time.
cues.zh: 我在2019年确诊，那时我49岁。

cues.en: I remember my oncologist telling me:
cues.zh: 我记得肿瘤科医生告诉我这个消息时说：

cues.en: "So you're probably looking at a year and a half of treatment."
cues.zh: “所以你可能要接受一年半的治疗。”

cues.en: And in my head, I was saying, "Who's got a year and a half to give to cancer?"
cues.zh: 但我心里想的是：“谁能拿出一年半的时间给癌症？”

cues.en: I'll give it six months, but after that, I really need to be cracking on with things, as if I had some control over it.
cues.zh: 我给它六个月，但之后我真的得继续生活，好像一切还在我的掌控之中。

cues.en: I went through treatment, and I had seen people out racing in dragon boats on this piece of water in Dublin that I passed sporadically
cues.zh: 治疗期间，我曾看到有人在都柏林这片水域上划龙舟比赛；我偶尔会经过那里，

cues.en: and thinking, that looks fantastic.
cues.zh: 心想：看起来真棒。

cues.en: And I remember noticing that it was all women in the boat that I saw, and I was kind of wondering what that club is.
cues.zh: 我记得我注意到，看到的船上全是女性，于是有点好奇那是什么俱乐部。

cues.en: And then during my cancer treatment, somebody mentioned to me the Plurabelle Paddlers, who were a breast cancer dragon boat team.
cues.zh: 后来在治疗期间，有人向我提到 Plurabelle Paddlers，那是一支乳腺癌患者龙舟队。

cues.en: So, when I got towards the end of my treatment, I looked it up on the website and signed up for a trial,
cues.zh: 治疗接近尾声时，我在网站上查了查，报名参加试训，

cues.en: and it was absolutely the best thing that I ever did and the best thing to come out of the cancer diagnosis and treatment.
cues.zh: 这是我做过最棒的决定，也是癌症诊断和治疗带来的最好结果。

cues.en: Where breast cancer dragon boat came from.
cues.zh: 乳腺癌龙舟运动的起源。

cues.en: Dragon boating itself is over 2,000 years old and it originated in China, and it's a really growing sport.
cues.zh: 龙舟运动本身已有两千多年历史，起源于中国，如今正日益普及。

cues.en: But a fabulous man in Canada, Dr. Don McKenzie, who was a sports medicine specialist,
cues.zh: 但加拿大有一位了不起的人，运动医学专家唐·麦肯齐博士，

cues.en: wanted to try out if dragon boating and repetitive upper body and arm exercises
cues.zh: 想研究龙舟运动以及反复的上肢和手臂锻炼，

cues.en: would help women in recovery from breast cancer to regrow their upper body strength after treatment.
cues.zh: 是否能帮助乳腺癌康复女性在治疗后恢复上肢力量。

cues.en: in a pilot with 25 women in Canada.
cues.zh: 在加拿大对25名女性开展了一项试点研究。

cues.en: And of course, what he discovered was that not only was it fantastic for rebuilding their upper-body strength
cues.zh: 当然，他发现这不仅非常有助于她们重建上肢力量，

cues.en: but emotionally, physically, socially, it was just fantastic for the women in every way.
cues.zh: 在情感、身体和社交层面，这对女性各方面都非常有益。

cues.en: And then the first world competition for breast cancer teams happened in Canada.
cues.zh: 随后，首届乳腺癌团队世界大赛在加拿大举行。

cues.en: Through the growing sport, it's now gone all over the world.
cues.zh: 随着这项运动发展壮大，如今它已遍及全球。

cues.en: How does it feel to be paddling alongside women that have had a very similar journey to you?
cues.zh: 和经历过相似历程的女性一起划船，感觉如何？

cues.en: Do you know, we joke all the time that we're all in the same boat, literally.
cues.zh: 你知道，我们总是开玩笑说，字面意义上我们都在同一条船上。

cues.en: There are women of every shape and size and age and colour and creed.
cues.zh: 这些女性有着不同的体形、身材、年龄、肤色和信仰。

cues.en: You know, we have differences across everything else, and then there's this one major thing that binds us all.
cues.zh: 我们在其他方面各不相同，但有一件大事把我们所有人联系在一起。

cues.en: And I'm not going to lie, yesterday I got a bit emotional, like looking around the lake
cues.zh: 说实话，昨天我有些激动，我环顾湖面时，

cues.en: and looking around the site and going, every one of us, every single one of us has gone through this journey.
cues.zh: 又环顾现场，心想我们每一个人，真的每一个人，都经历过这段旅程。

cues.en: There is a shorthand that we have with each other because we understand what people have been through, the journey they've gone on.
cues.zh: 我们彼此之间有一种默契，因为我们了解对方经历过什么、走过怎样的历程。

cues.en: And there's something we share and know about each other that others, with the best will in the world
cues.zh: 我们共享着一些只有彼此才能理解的东西，即使别人再有善意，

cues.en: can't understand what it might be to get a cancer diagnosis, to have to go through treatment.
cues.zh: 也无法理解得知癌症诊断、不得不接受治疗是什么感受。

cues.en: And I really see it that we all took those lemons and we made lemonade.
cues.zh: 我真心觉得，我们都把那些柠檬变成了柠檬水。

cues.en: What message do you hope people take away when they see you paddling?
cues.zh: 你希望人们看到你们划船时得到什么启示？

cues.en: There is no family anywhere in the world now, really, that hasn't been impacted by cancer.
cues.zh: 如今，世界上几乎没有哪个家庭未曾受到癌症影响。

cues.en: And what I'd love for them to take from seeing 4,500 women on a lake in France, paddling and living their best lives
cues.zh: 我希望他们看到法国湖面上4500名女性划船、享受美好生活时，

cues.en: is that there are positive stories. Of course, there is loss, but there is life, and there is a way
cues.zh: 明白其中有许多积极的故事。当然会有失去，但也有生命，也有办法

cues.en: to get back your strength, your health, your happiness.
cues.zh: 重新找回力量、健康和幸福。

cues.en: And, you know, we're looking for support. We're not looking for pity.
cues.zh: 我们寻求的是支持，而不是怜悯。

cues.en: And we're looking for support for us to live our best lives.
cues.zh: 我们希望得到支持，去过好自己的生活。

cues.en: And I have to say that phrase has been used so many times by members of the club
cues.zh: 我得说，俱乐部成员们已经多次说起这句话，

cues.en: as we wander around France here in between trainings, you know, stopping and having an ice cream.
cues.zh: 我们在法国训练间隙四处走走，停下来吃个冰淇淋时也会说起。

cues.en: We just really appreciate that we're living our best lives and that we've been supported
cues.zh: 我们非常珍惜自己正在过着最好的生活，也珍惜得到的支持，

cues.en: to make the best of our lives, however long that may be
cues.zh: 让我们无论还能拥有多久，都尽力过好生活，

cues.en: and it will be different for everybody.
cues.zh: 而这对每个人来说都不一样。

cues.en: Maria Fleming. Now, plastic probably isn't the first ingredient you think of when you're making some cookies.
cues.zh: 玛丽亚·弗莱明。现在，塑料大概不是你做饼干时首先想到的食材。

cues.en: In fact, plastic probably is not in your recipe at all.
cues.zh: 事实上，塑料根本不在你的食谱里。

cues.en: However, researchers in the United States are working on a recipe for cookies made from recycled plastic bottles.
cues.zh: 然而，美国研究人员正在研究一种用回收塑料瓶制作饼干的配方。

cues.en: Mary Roeloffs from Forbes magazine spoke to my colleague Reegini Vardinathan.
cues.zh: 《福布斯》杂志的玛丽·罗洛夫斯接受了我同事里吉尼·瓦尔迪纳坦的采访。

cues.en: It's important to note that humans aren't eating raw plastic, even in these cookies.
cues.zh: 需要指出的是，即使在这些饼干中，人类吃的也不是未经处理的塑料。

cues.en: Microbes, you know, like bacteria and algae, are eating the plastic and then breaking it down into the nutritional molecules
cues.zh: 微生物，比如细菌和藻类，会吞噬塑料并将其分解成营养分子，

cues.en: that we think of as proteins, fats and vitamins.
cues.zh: 也就是蛋白质、脂肪和维生素等。

cues.en: And then more yeast are reassembling those things back into a food product.
cues.zh: 然后，更多酵母会把这些物质重新组装成食品。

cues.en: And then a 3D printer is actually turning the final mixture into a little cookie that's reportedly quite nutrient-dense.
cues.zh: 接着，3D打印机会把最终混合物制成一块据报道营养相当丰富的小饼干。

cues.en: Have you tried one? I have not.
cues.zh: 你试过一块吗？我没有。

cues.en: They are not doing full-scale taste testing yet.
cues.zh: 他们还没有进行全面的味觉测试。

cues.en: They're still waiting for sign-off, but they have done some smell tests, and apparently most participants said that they would eat the cookies
cues.zh: 他们仍在等待批准，但已经做过一些嗅觉测试，据说大多数参与者表示会吃这种饼干。

cues.en: in a resource-limited setting. These are supposed to be quite good for you, aren't they?
cues.zh: 在资源有限的环境下，据说这种饼干对身体相当有益，对吧？

cues.en: Which to most people might sound counterintuitive, certainly to me.
cues.zh: 这对大多数人来说听起来可能违反直觉，至少对我来说是这样。

cues.en: I think there's protein and vitamins and fats, and in the future they said they're hoping that they'll be able to
cues.zh: 我想其中有蛋白质、维生素和脂肪；他们说，未来希望能够

cues.en: make the starch and the fiber and the sweetener and everything, really, using this microbe process that they've come up with.
cues.zh: 真正利用他们研发的微生物工艺制造淀粉、纤维、甜味剂等所有成分。

cues.en: And what's the reasoning behind this? It was conducted as part of a NASA-led project aimed at creating foods for deep-space exploration.
cues.zh: 那这样做的原因是什么？这项研究是美国国家航空航天局牵头项目的一部分，旨在为深空探索制造食物。

cues.en: Astronauts could be among the earliest adopters, but they could also be used in disaster zones.
cues.zh: 宇航员可能会成为最早使用者，灾区也可能用得上这种食品。

cues.en: On submarines, or other places where fresh foods are harder to get.
cues.zh: 它还可以用于潜艇，或其他难以获得新鲜食物的地方。

cues.en: And this isn't the first time that plastic's been used for food in this way, is it?
cues.zh: 这也不是塑料第一次以这种方式用于食品，对吧？

cues.en: I think scientists have achieved this before, but on a bit of a smaller scale.
cues.zh: 我想科学家以前实现过这一点，只是规模小一些。

cues.en: So, an Edinburgh study a few years ago was able to convert plastic water bottles into vanilla flavouring.
cues.zh: 几年前，爱丁堡的一项研究就曾将塑料水瓶转化为香草调味剂。

cues.en: But researchers in the US have also been able to engineer a fungus that's capable of eating things like styrofoam and foam cups and packaging
cues.zh: 但美国研究人员还成功培育出一种真菌，能够吞食泡沫塑料、泡沫杯和包装材料等物质，

cues.en: to help break down those materials.
cues.zh: 从而帮助分解这些材料。

cues.en: And why would you do this in the first place?
cues.zh: 那最初为什么要这样做呢？

cues.en: I think being able to do this might help bolster the global food
cues.zh: 我认为，这样做可能大大有助于增强全球粮食

cues.en: supply as demand continues to surge.
cues.zh: 全球食品供应，因为需求仍在不断激增。

cues.en: Mary Roeloffs. Coming up on The Happy Pod,
cues.zh: 玛丽·罗洛夫斯。接下来，《快乐播客》将带来……

cues.en: those small victories of introducing Synergy to someone and they previously were unwilling to work with us
cues.zh: 那些小小的胜利：把 Synergy 介绍给一些人，他们之前不愿与我们合作。

cues.en: to get their documents, but because of her being there, they're willing.
cues.zh: 他们本不愿提供证件，但因为 Synergy 在场，他们愿意了。

cues.en: The mini pig helping to combat homelessness in Washington, D.C.
cues.zh: 这头迷你小猪帮助应对华盛顿特区的无家可归问题。

cues.en: You're listening to The Happy Pod.
cues.zh: 你正在收听《快乐播客》。

cues.en: A community in the north of England is on a mission to bring together multiple generations,
cues.zh: 英格兰北部的一个社区致力于让不同世代走到一起，

cues.en: so they've built a nursery inside a retirement living facility.
cues.zh: 因此，他们在一处养老居住设施内建起了托儿所。

cues.en: The owners say everyone has something to offer, no matter their age.
cues.zh: 业主们说，无论年龄大小，每个人都有所贡献。

cues.en: The BBC's Maira Anubi has been along to find out more.
cues.zh: BBC 记者 Maira Anubi 前往那里了解更多情况。

cues.en: I've just stepped into a bright, open area that has both a reception and cafe.
cues.zh: 我刚走进一处明亮开阔的区域，那里既有接待处，也有咖啡馆。

cues.en: This place is called Belong. It's a retirement village, basically a building with apartments and rooms for older people
cues.zh: 这里叫 Belong，是一座养老村，本质上是一栋为老人提供公寓和房间的建筑，

cues.en: who are either living independently or need more care and support.
cues.zh: 他们有的能独立生活，有的则需要更多照护和支持。

cues.en: There also happens to be a nursery here.
cues.zh: 这里恰好还设有一所托儿所。

cues.en: I've been invited to a room where there are about 20 people,
cues.zh: 我受邀来到一间房，里面大约有20个人，

cues.en: so the older folks, support workers, children,
cues.zh: 包括老人、工作人员和孩子，

cues.en: and they're all sat on chairs in a big circle for one of their shared activities.
cues.zh: 他们都围坐在椅子上，参加一项共同活动。

cues.en: So right now, they're having a session where one man has brought in different reptiles
cues.zh: 现在，他们正在进行一场活动：一名男子带来了各种爬行动物，

cues.en: and everyone is having a go touching them, and it's fascinating.
cues.zh: 大家轮流触摸它们，场面非常有趣。

cues.en: Nice to meet you. What's your name? Frieda.
cues.zh: 很高兴认识你。你叫什么名字？弗里达。

cues.en: Frieda, how did you find today's session with the reptiles?
cues.zh: 弗里达，你觉得今天和爬行动物一起的活动怎么样？

cues.en: Very interesting.
cues.zh: 非常有趣。

cues.en: And how do you find interacting with the kids?
cues.zh: 和孩子们互动，你感觉怎么样？

cues.en: I do enjoy being with the children. They're so enthusiastic about things, aren't they?
cues.zh: 我很喜欢和孩子们在一起。他们对什么都那么热情，对吧？

cues.en: And you just... you just get drawn in, and sort of enjoy being with them, really.
cues.zh: 你会不知不觉被吸引进去，真的就喜欢和他们待在一起。

cues.en: Yes. Could you tell me your name and, if you would, I know you look really young, but how old you are?
cues.zh: 是的。可以告诉我你的名字吗？虽然你看起来很年轻，但如果方便的话，你多大了？

cues.en: I'm 69. My name is Ann.
cues.zh: 我69岁。我叫 Ann。

cues.en: I think it's wonderful with children that they have opportunity to chat to the older people.
cues.zh: 我觉得孩子们有机会和老人聊天非常好。

cues.en: I like to come and see what the children are doing. They ask some fascinating questions.
cues.zh: 我喜欢过来看看孩子们在做什么。他们会问一些非常有趣的问题。

cues.en: They're finding out and you're finding out. It's lovely.
cues.zh: 他们在了解，你也在了解。这很美好。

cues.en: Ann, are you going to come clean now? Oh, my God.
cues.zh: Ann，你现在要坦白了吗？天哪。

cues.en: You told everybody you were 69, and how old are you really?
cues.zh: 你告诉大家你69岁，那你到底多大了？

cues.en: 85. And the person who knows their real age—well, that's Sue Egersdorff,
cues.zh: 85岁。而知道她真实年龄的人——就是 Sue Egersdorff，

cues.en: the co-founder of the charity that runs this nursery.
cues.zh: 她是运营这所托儿所的慈善机构联合创始人。

cues.en: Now, Sue saw a big need for a space that would let people mingle outside their own age group.
cues.zh: Sue 发现，人们非常需要一个能让不同年龄群体彼此交流的空间。

cues.en: What we see is, you know, a society which is becoming fragmented and people are becoming socially isolated.
cues.zh: 我们看到，社会正变得碎片化，人们也越来越与社会隔绝。

cues.en: How can we connect some of these things that have traditionally been quite separate and diverse?
cues.zh: 我们怎样才能把这些传统上相当分离、各不相同的事物联系起来？

cues.en: It all started when Sue noticed that residents at her own mother's care home seemed secluded from the wider community,
cues.zh: 一切始于 Sue 注意到，自己母亲所在的护理院居民似乎与更广泛的社区隔绝，

cues.en: even though they still had a lot more to give.
cues.zh: 尽管他们仍有许多东西可以贡献。

cues.en: It just felt like within the care settings, there was such diversity of knowledge and wisdom
cues.zh: 她只是觉得，在护理环境中蕴藏着如此多元的知识与智慧，

cues.en: that could be used to really help young children progress and see how they fitted into the world.
cues.zh: 这些知识与智慧本可以真正帮助孩子成长，并了解自己如何融入世界。

cues.en: Back in 2019, Sue and her co-founder, Liz Ludden, founded the charity Ready Generations
cues.zh: 2019年，Sue 与联合创始人 Liz Ludden 创办了 Ready Generations 慈善机构，

cues.en: to create a centre that would bring elderly people and young children together.
cues.zh: 旨在建立一个让老年人与幼儿走到一起的中心。

cues.en: So they approached Belong Villages, an organisation that runs retirement homes,
cues.zh: 于是，他们找到运营养老院的 Belong Villages，

cues.en: with the idea of putting a nursery in one of them.
cues.zh: 提出在其中一处养老院开设托儿所的想法。

cues.en: The nursery in Belong opened in 2022.
cues.zh: Belong 的托儿所于2022年开业。

cues.en: It started off with just two children, but word of this unusual place spread, and it's now full, with 25 children.
cues.zh: 这里最初只有两个孩子，但这处特别的地方逐渐传开，如今已经招满25个孩子。

cues.en: Alison is visiting her mother Dorothy, who lives at this retirement village,
cues.zh: Alison 正在探望住在这座养老村的母亲 Dorothy，

cues.en: and they both say they've seen a positive impact on both the kids and the older people.
cues.zh: 她们都说，这里对孩子和老人都有积极影响。

cues.en: To see people kneeling down on the floor, that is sensational.
cues.zh: 看着大家跪在地板上，真是太棒了。

cues.en: The kids make you forget the aches and... Oh, yes. Yes. Yes.
cues.zh: 孩子们会让你忘记疼痛……哦，是的，是的，是的。

cues.en: The nursery has brought a lot of pleasure and interest.
cues.zh: 这家托儿所带来了许多快乐和兴趣。

cues.en: They learn to care and share, which I think is very important.
cues.zh: 他们学会关心和分享，我认为这非常重要。

cues.en: That report was from Maira Anubi.
cues.zh: 以上报道来自梅拉·阿努比。

cues.en: A man here in London has become the first person in the world to undergo live AI-assisted brain surgery.
cues.zh: 伦敦一名男子成为全球首位接受实时AI辅助脑部手术的人。

cues.en: Rhys Hibbert could have lost his sight had a tumour not been removed from his pituitary gland that contains vital hormones.
cues.zh: 如果不从含有重要激素的垂体腺中切除肿瘤，里斯·希伯特可能会失明。

cues.en: My colleague Sarah Montague spoke to Professor Hani Marcus, who performed the operation.
cues.zh: 我的同事莎拉·蒙塔古采访了主刀的哈尼·马库斯教授。

cues.en: The gland sits more or less in the centre of the brain, and although it's not cancer, these tumours grow and grow and grow,
cues.zh: 这个腺体大致位于大脑中央；虽然肿瘤不是癌症，却会不断生长。

cues.en: and eventually put pressure on the sort of associated structures, including those that supply his vision.
cues.zh: 最终，它们会压迫相关结构，包括负责供给视觉的结构。

cues.en: And in this particular case, he was losing his eyesight.
cues.zh: 而在他的具体病例中，他当时正在失去视力。

cues.en: Yes. Yes. Tell us how this AI tool helped when you were removing the tumour.
cues.zh: 是的，是的。请说说，切除肿瘤时，这款AI工具如何提供帮助。

cues.en: We do this operation using a tiny camera placed through the nose
cues.zh: 手术时，我们会把一枚微型摄像头从鼻腔放入，

cues.en: then looking at a screen to recognise the structures at the base of the brain.
cues.zh: 然后看着屏幕，努力辨认大脑底部的结构。

cues.en: And sometimes it's obvious, but sometimes it can be very challenging.
cues.zh: 有时这些结构很明显，但有时辨认起来非常困难。

cues.en: Partly because these structures are covered by bone, but also because the tumour itself can deform these structures,
cues.zh: 一部分原因是这些结构被骨头覆盖，另一部分是肿瘤本身会使它们变形，

cues.en: and so the AI acted as a sort of co-pilot assistant adjacent to the primary screen,
cues.zh: 因此，AI就像主屏幕旁的副驾驶助手，

cues.en: identifying the structures that we care most about—the blood vessels and the tumour itself.
cues.zh: 它会标出我们最关心的结构——血管和肿瘤本身。

cues.en: So, what it has effectively is knowledge of a model of a brain or of your patient's brain,
cues.zh: 所以，实际上，它掌握了一个大脑模型，或是你这位患者的大脑模型，

cues.en: and while you're operating, it is guiding you?
cues.zh: 也就是说，你手术时它会为你提供引导？

cues.en: It's been trained on many, many operations in the past, hundreds of operations, and so it knows very well what an operation should look like.
cues.zh: 它接受过许多、许多过去手术的训练，数量达数百例，因此非常清楚手术应该是什么样子。

cues.en: With that training, when it looks at the operation in real time, it can identify a structure and say, "I think this is that."
cues.zh: 有了这些训练，它实时观察手术时，就能识别结构并说：“我认为这就是那个结构。”

cues.en: It's an assistant that often just confirms what you think,
cues.zh: 它只是辅助工具，通常只是确认你的判断，

cues.en: but it's an additional safety measure, and we think can help patients have a more safe operation.
cues.zh: 但它是额外的安全措施，我们认为能帮助患者更安全地接受手术。

cues.en: Okay, so what, as you are there with your scalpel, yes, a voice is saying from the AI tool, "Oops, don't do that."
cues.zh: 那么，当你拿着手术刀时，AI工具会不会在旁边说：“糟糕，别这么做”？

cues.en: It's on the screen rather than a voice, but yes, exactly that.
cues.zh: 它不是用声音，而是在屏幕上显示，但确实如此。

cues.en: It annotates the live video feed and will draw around the structures as it recognises them when you ask it.
cues.zh: 它会标注实时视频画面；你要求时，还会在识别出的结构周围画圈。

cues.en: Okay, so you're using the screen as a guide whether to move left or to move right?
cues.zh: 所以，你是在用屏幕引导自己向左或向右移动？

cues.en: Yes, well, we do the operation as usual, and then at key points, the most important parts of the operation,
cues.zh: 是的，我们照常进行手术，然后在关键节点——手术最重要的部分——停下来，

cues.en: we would usually stop and reassess to make sure that we understand where everything is and don't make a mistake.
cues.zh: 我们通常会重新评估，确保了解一切所在，并且不会犯错。

cues.en: And at those points, that's when the AI is most helpful, because it provides an additional check to make sure the surgeon's got everything right.
cues.zh: 而在这些节点，AI最有帮助，因为它提供额外检查，确保外科医生判断无误。

cues.en: Most people now use GPS when they drive,
cues.zh: 这就像现在大多数人开车都会使用GPS，

cues.en: But the AI co-pilot is like someone beside you, looking through the windscreen and warning you if you might miss a turn.
cues.zh: 但有了AI副驾驶，就像旁边有人透过挡风玻璃看路，提醒你可能错过转弯。

cues.en: Okay, now, given this extra expertise, was it the most successful, the best operation you've ever done?
cues.zh: 那么，有了这份额外专业支持，这是你做过最成功、最好的一次手术吗？

cues.en: Yes, it went really well. I'm very happy to say, and I'm most pleased that he's made such a good recovery.
cues.zh: 是的，手术非常顺利。我很高兴这么说，也最欣慰他恢复得这么好。

cues.en: Okay, so we should say, for him, he was losing his sight. Now...
cues.zh: 我们应该说明，他当时正在失去视力。现在……

cues.en: Yes, it's back to normal. He's fully back to normal, too.
cues.zh: 是的，现在视力恢复正常，他本人也完全恢复正常。

cues.en: So, the point of the AI is that it allows you to remove more of the tumour and do less damage?
cues.zh: 所以，AI的作用是让你能切除更多肿瘤，同时减少损伤？

cues.en: Yes, I think it's most important for safety reasons.
cues.zh: 是的，我认为它最重要的意义在于安全。

cues.en: So, the structures there are so delicate that if you make an error, even perhaps by a few millimetres, you can cause great injury to a patient.
cues.zh: 这些结构非常脆弱，即使只差几毫米，也可能对患者造成严重伤害。

cues.en: And we're very careful surgeons, both to have looked at a patient's scan and be very cautious during the operation itself.
cues.zh: 我们外科医生非常谨慎，会查看患者扫描结果，并在手术中格外小心。

cues.en: But it's any tool that can help you be even more safe to make sure these structures are protected is greatly appreciated.
cues.zh: 任何能让你更加安全、确保这些结构受到保护的工具，都非常宝贵。

cues.en: So, this, do you think this is now the way forward for most surgeries?
cues.zh: 那么，你认为这会成为大多数手术今后的发展方向吗？

cues.en: I think it's the very first step, but I'm bullish that in the next five or ten years
cues.zh: 我认为这只是第一步，但我乐观地相信，未来五到十年，

cues.en: this will make as much impact in surgery as it's made outside of surgery.
cues.zh: 它对手术的影响会和它在手术之外产生的影响一样大。

cues.en: Having used it, I'm confident a surgeon using this sort of AI will do better, make better decisions and have a better operation than one not using AI.
cues.zh: 我亲自使用过它，因此相信采用这类AI的外科医生会做得更好，作出更好的决定，手术效果也会优于不用AI的医生。

cues.en: Professor Hani Marcus speaking to Sarah Montague.
cues.zh: Hani Marcus教授接受Sarah Montague采访。

cues.en: We end in Washington, D.C., where a small pig is being...
cues.zh: 我们最后来到华盛顿特区，那里有一头小猪正在被用于……

cues.en: used as part of a campaign to help people experiencing homelessness.
cues.zh: 用于一项帮助无家可归者的行动。

cues.en: The Happy Pod's Rylee Farrell has been to meet her.
cues.zh: 《Happy Pod》的莱莉·法雷尔去见了她。

cues.en: I'm in Washington, D.C.'s Union Station, a historic travel hub, just a jog from the US Capitol.
cues.zh: 我在华盛顿特区的联合车站，这座历史悠久的交通枢纽距离美国国会大厦仅几步之遥。

cues.en: Under vaulted ceilings decorated with gold leaf, travelers bustle towards trains and buses.
cues.zh: 在饰有金箔的拱顶下，旅客匆忙赶往火车和公交车。

cues.en: Locals and out-of-towners shuffle across the white granite floor. It's business as usual, except.
cues.zh: 当地人和外地人穿过白色花岗岩地面。一切一如往常，只是……

cues.en: Hi, this is Synergy. Cool. Synergy? Synergy. Yeah, she works with the unhoused for humanization.
cues.zh: 嗨，这是赛能吉。酷。赛能吉？赛能吉。没错，她和无家可归者一起工作，帮助他们恢复人的尊严。

cues.en: Meet Synergy, a 2-kilogram pig. Her toenails are painted red, and she's turning heads.
cues.zh: 认识一下赛能吉，一头两公斤重的小猪。她的脚趾甲涂成红色，吸引了众人的目光。

cues.en: But she offers more than entertainment. Synergy is training to become a therapy animal.
cues.zh: 但她不只是供人娱乐。赛能吉正在接受训练，准备成为一只治疗动物。

cues.en: She also works as a wellness ambassador for people experiencing homelessness. She's part of a crisis intervention nonprofit called the H3 Project.
cues.zh: 她还担任无家可归者的健康大使。她属于一家名为 H3 Project 的危机干预非营利组织。

cues.en: She works with the unhoused. Train stations like Union Station often attract people who are experiencing homelessness.
cues.zh: 她在这里帮助无家可归者。联合车站这样的火车站经常吸引无家可归的人。

cues.en: They are public places that offer shelter from extreme weather and access to restrooms.
cues.zh: 这些公共场所能让人躲避极端天气，也能使用洗手间。

cues.en: It's also where Dr Amy Angel spends most of her time. She works with the unhoused here at Union Station.
cues.zh: 这也是艾米·安格尔博士大部分时间工作的地方。她在联合车站帮助无家可归者。

cues.en: We'll be walking along and two people, you know, the thuggish type, who'd never stop and talk, suddenly say, "Oh, my God! Is that a pig?"
cues.zh: 我们走着走着，两个看起来有些凶悍的人——他们本来绝不会停下来交谈——突然会说：“天哪！那是一头猪吗？”

cues.en: Next to two non-English speakers and a homeless person, a group that would never otherwise mix is talking, all looking at the same thing,
cues.zh: 两个不会说英语的人、一个无家可归者，还有这群本来不会相聚的人，竟一起交谈，所有人都看着同一个东西。

cues.en: And that's what's amazing. She just breaks down those barriers.
cues.zh: 这正是神奇之处。她就这样打破了那些隔阂。

cues.en: She founded the H3 Project. The name stands for Home, Health, and Happiness.
cues.zh: 她创立了 H3 Project。这个名称代表“家园、健康和幸福”。

cues.en: And as we make our way through the station, Synergy is about to make a new friend. It's a pig.
cues.zh: 我们穿过车站时，赛能吉要结交一位新朋友了。她是一头猪。

cues.en: Have you seen her yet? You met her? I have never. Hi, how are you? I mean, this is Synergy.
cues.zh: 你见过她吗？你认识她吗？我从没见过。嗨，你好吗？我是说，这就是赛能吉。

cues.en: For Amy, moments like that are exactly why Synergy is there.
cues.zh: 对艾米来说，这样的时刻正是赛能吉来到这里的原因。

cues.en: Synergy was just a concept because I had heard how smart pigs are.
cues.zh: 赛能吉最初只是一个想法，因为我听说猪非常聪明。

cues.en: So I was just looking for an idea that would help to have a different approach,
cues.zh: 所以我只是想找一个想法，采取不同的方式，

cues.en: to have something to open up that conversation, someone maybe that's resistant to case management,
cues.zh: 找个契机开启对话，接触那些可能抗拒个案管理的人，

cues.en: have that outside-of-the-box type of thing that might engage them with us.
cues.zh: 用这种突破常规的方式，让他们愿意和我们接触。

cues.en: Amy founded H3 in January 2020. First four months of COVID, I worked every single day.
cues.zh: 艾米于2020年1月创立 H3。新冠疫情开始的头四个月，我每天都在工作。

cues.en: Right behind Union Station were 67 tents and 78 individuals. I knew them all and their stories, because frankly nobody else was out there.
cues.zh: 就在联合车站后面，有67顶帐篷、78个人。我认识他们每一个人，知道他们的故事，因为说实话，当时那里没有其他人。

cues.en: People living out there felt forgotten and abandoned.
cues.zh: 住在那里的人感到自己被遗忘、被抛弃。

cues.en: In the past year, H3 says it has provided 93 housing matches and 217 Narcan administrations for overdose reversal.
cues.zh: H3称，过去一年已促成93次住房匹配，并进行了217次纳洛酮给药以逆转药物过量。

cues.en: A child doesn't grow up saying, "I want to experience homelessness," or "I want mental instability," or "a substance challenge."
cues.zh: 没有孩子长大后会说：“我想体验无家可归、精神不稳定，或药物滥用。”

cues.en: Life happens, trauma happens. Everyone out here has a reason. We can't understand it unless we dive into their story and see them as an individual,
cues.zh: 生活会发生变故，创伤也会发生。每个流落街头的人都有原因，除非深入了解其故事、把他们视为个体，否则无法理解。

cues.en: not just a number and not just a statistic, because they deserve that.
cues.zh: 而不只是一个数字或统计数据，因为他们值得被这样看待。

cues.en: What motivates me is those small things, those small wins.
cues.zh: 激励我的，是那些小事、那些小小的胜利。

cues.en: I mean, obviously, I want the big wins.
cues.zh: 当然，我也希望取得大的胜利。

cues.en: I want the person getting employed.
cues.zh: 我希望有人能够找到工作。

cues.en: I want the person who finally was able to get his high school diploma at age 34.
cues.zh: 我希望有人终于能在34岁拿到高中毕业证书。

cues.en: I want everyone in housing.
cues.zh: 我希望每个人都有住房。

cues.en: I want those big wins, but I also have to take time, appreciate, and really celebrate those small wins,
cues.zh: 我希望取得那些大的胜利，但也要花时间去珍惜、真正庆祝那些小小的胜利，

cues.en: those small victories, and that's what really even Synergy brings in, because those small victories
cues.zh: 那些小小的成功；赛能吉带来的正是这些小小的成功，

cues.en: of introducing Synergy to someone and they previously were unwilling to work with us to get their documents,
cues.zh: 比如把赛能吉介绍给某个人，原本他不愿意和我们合作办理证件，

cues.en: but because of her being there, they're willing, and that's a win to me.
cues.zh: 但因为她在场，对方愿意了，这对我来说就是胜利。

cues.en: Just know, the most important thing to do when you see someone experiencing homelessness is to acknowledge them.
cues.zh: 请记住，看到无家可归者时，最重要的是认可他们、和他们打招呼。

cues.en: Smiles go a long way, and looking at someone is like, "How are you doing today?" or "Good morning." Little things like that
cues.zh: 一个微笑很有帮助，看着对方问一句“你今天好吗？”或“早上好”，这样的小事

cues.en: Can literally make or break someone's day, especially when they're on the street.
cues.zh: 真的可能让一个人的一天变好或变糟，尤其是当他们流落街头时。

cues.en: That was Rylee Farrell reporting.
cues.zh: 以上是莱莉·法雷尔的报道。

cues.en: And that's all from The Happy Pod for now.
cues.zh: 以上就是本期《Happy Pod》的全部内容。

cues.en: We'd love to hear from you. As ever, the address is globalpodcast@bbc.co.uk.
cues.zh: 我们期待听到你的来信。地址一如既往，是 globalpodcast@bbc.co.uk。

cues.en: The editor of this edition is Karen Martin.
cues.zh: 本期编辑是凯伦·马丁。

cues.en: I'm Holly Gibbs. Until next time, goodbye.
cues.zh: 我是霍莉·吉布斯。下期再见。
